units.title: Introduction to Enzymes and Classification
units.topics: Activity 1: Identification of enzymes • Task: Identify enzymes involved in everyday activities and classify them as per enzyme classification • Real-Life Problem Addressed: Understanding how enzymes improve efficiency in household and industrial processes • Expected Outcome: Students will be able to classify enzymes and correlate enzyme specificity with practical applications. Activity 2: Digestive Enzyme Case Study • Task: Study digestive enzyme formulations available in the market and identify enzymes used for digestion of proteins, fats, and carbohydrates. • Real life problem addressed: Digestive disorders and reduced enzyme secretion in humans. • Expected Outcome: Students will correlate enzyme function with human digestive health. Activity 3: Match the Enzyme Puzzle • Task: Solve a matching activity connecting enzymes with substrates, cofactors, products, and industrial applications. • Real life problem addressed: Need for rapid identification of enzyme functions in biotechnology and healthcare. • Expected Outcome: Students will strengthen conceptual understanding of enzyme properties and biochemical roles.

units.title: Enzyme Kinetics
units.topics: Activity 1: Michaelis–Menten Numerical Tutorial • Task: Calculate Km and Vmax values using experimental enzyme activity data and interpret enzyme efficiency. • Real life problem addressed: Optimization of enzyme activity in pharmaceutical and industrial production processes. • Expected Outcome: Students will apply enzyme kinetics principles for analyzing catalytic efficiency. Activity 2: Fever and Enzyme Activity Case Study • Task: Analyze the effect of fever and hypothermia on enzyme-controlled metabolic reactions in the human body. • Real life problem addressed: Impact of abnormal body temperature on metabolism and health. • Expected Outcome: Students will explain the effect of temperature on enzyme activity and stability. Activity 3: Lineweaver–Burk Plot Assignment • Task: Construct a Lineweaver–Burk plot using provided data and determine kinetic parameters. • Real life problem addressed: Use of enzyme kinetics in drug development and industrial bioprocess optimization. • Expected Outcome: Students will interpret enzyme kinetic graphs and compare enzyme performance.

units.title: Coenzymes, Regulation and Enzyme Inhibition
units.topics: Activity 1: Drug–Enzyme Interaction Case Study • Task: Study the mechanism of action of drugs such as penicillin, aspirin, or sulfa drugs and identify the type of enzyme inhibition involved. • Real life problem addressed: Use of enzyme inhibitors in disease treatment and antibiotic therapy. • Expected Outcome: Students will understand clinical applications of enzyme inhibition. Activity 2: Vitamin Deficiency and Coenzyme Assignment • Task: Prepare a presentation explaining the role of vitamin-derived coenzymes and disorders caused by vitamin deficiencies. • Real life problem addressed: Nutritional deficiencies affecting metabolic pathways and public health. • Expected Outcome: Students will correlate vitamins, coenzymes, and metabolic disorders. Activity 3: Enzyme Regulation Quiz • Task: Participate in a quiz covering allosteric regulation, feedback inhibition, isoenzymes, and inhibition mechanisms. • Real life problem addressed: Importance of enzyme regulation in maintaining metabolic balance. • Expected Outcome: Students will differentiate various regulatory mechanisms of enzymes.

units.title: Enzyme Purification and Immobilization
units.topics: Activity 1: Enzyme Purification Flowchart Assignment • Task: Design a stepwise flowchart for purification of an industrial enzyme from microbial culture. • Real life problem addressed: Need for efficient purification methods in pharmaceutical and food industries. • Expected Outcome: Students will understand stages involved in enzyme extraction and purification. Activity 2: Immobilized Enzyme Industrial Case Study • Task: Study applications of immobilized enzymes in lactose-free milk production, biosensors, or glucose monitoring systems. • Real life problem addressed: Need for reusable and stable enzymes in industrial and medical applications. • Expected Outcome: Students will evaluate benefits and industrial importance of enzyme immobilization. Activity 3: Chromatography Technique Tutorial • Task: Compare chromatography techniques such as ion exchange, gel filtration, and affinity chromatography based on principle and applications. • Real life problem addressed: Selection of suitable purification techniques for biomolecule separation. • Expected Outcome: Students will differentiate purification methods and justify their industrial use.

units.title: Stability Analysis and Frequency Response Analysis
units.topics: Activity 1: Frequency response and Bode Plot • Task: Generate a Bode Plot (Magnitude and Phase) for a second-order process. Identify the Gain Margin (GM) and Phase Margin (PM). • Real life problem addressed: In a biochemical plant, sensor noise can cause "chatter" in control valves. Engineers must ensure the system doesn't amplify this noise. • Expected Outcome: Students apply the Bode stability criterion to determine how "close" a system is to instability and evaluate its robustness against process delays. Activity 2: Stability Analysis Comparison • Task: Study and compare various stability analysis methods. • Real life problem addressed: Need of such methods and best used in industrial and medical applications. • Expected Outcome: Students will evaluate benefits and industrial importance of stability analysis methods. Activity 3: Numerical Solving • Task: Solve problems using various stability methods. • Real life problem addressed: Selection of suitable method • Expected Outcome: Students will numerical solving skills and justify their answers with stability check.

units.title: Hypothesis Testing
units.topics: Null and Alternative Hypotheses, Type I and Type II Errors, P-values and Significance Level One-tailed vs. Two-tailed Tests, Confidence Intervals Tutorial Activity: Formulating hypotheses and interpreting p-values in different research scenarios. Mapping of Course Outcomes for Unit IV ➢ CO 1: Select and apply appropriate statistical methods for analysing different types of biological data. ■ (Hypothesis testing is a key method for biological data analysis.) ➢ CO 2: Interpret and communicate statistical findings effectively. ■ (Understanding p-values, significance levels, and confidence intervals relates to interpreting findings.) ➢ CO 5: Design and conduct basic statistical studies. ■ (Formulating hypotheses is a foundational step in designing research studies.)

units.title: Comparing Means
